why.en: A modal verb is always followed by the base verb — no "to", no "s".
why.bn: Modal verb-এর পরে সবসময় base verb বসে — কোনো "to" না, কোনো "s" না।

q.en: "The exam was tight, but I ___ finish it in time yesterday." (one specific past success)
q.bn: "The exam was tight, but I ___ finish it in time yesterday." (একটা specific past success)

why.en: For one specific past achievement, use "was/were able to", not "could" (which is for general past ability).
why.bn: একটা specific past achievement-এর জন্য "was/were able to" লাগে, "could" না (যেটা general past ability-এর জন্য)।

q.en: "You ___ come to the party if you don't want to — it's totally optional."
q.bn: "You ___ come to the party if you don't want to — it's totally optional."

why.en: "Don't have to" means no obligation (optional). "Mustn't" would mean it's forbidden, which is the opposite meaning.
why.bn: "Don't have to" মানে obligation নেই (optional)। "Mustn't" মানে forbidden, যেটা উল্টো অর্থ।

q.en: "The lights are off and the car is gone — they ___ be home." (strong evidence they are NOT home)
q.bn: "The lights are off and the car is gone — they ___ be home." (তারা বাসায় নেই, এমন strong evidence)

why.en: "Can't" expresses near-certainty that something is NOT true, based on evidence.
why.bn: "Can't" প্রায় নিশ্চিত যে কিছু সত্য নয়, evidence-এর ভিত্তিতে।

q.en: Fix: "She must has forgotten her keys."
q.bn: ঠিক করো: "She must has forgotten her keys."

options.en: She must have forgotten her keys.
options.bn: She must have forgotten her keys.

options.en: She must had forgotten her keys.
options.bn: She must had forgotten her keys.

why.en: Past deduction is always "modal + have + past participle" — never "must has".
why.bn: Past deduction সবসময় "modal + have + past participle" — "must has" কখনো না।
